nodes.title: Quartic pair counts with finite local conditions
nodes.statement: For integral pairs of ternary quadratic forms in a G_Z-invariant union S of finitely many residue classes, count absolutely irreducible orbits with 0<|Disc|<X in real signature i=0,1,2. Then N_i(S;X)=C_i X nu(S)+o_S(X), with normalized coefficient Haar measures, C_i=zeta(2)^2 zeta(3)/(2 n_i) and (n_0,n_1,n_2)=(24,4,8). Absolutely irreducible means the quartic field has S4 closure. This is not an all-etale-orbit count. Here nu(S) is the actual proportion of allowed coefficient residues modulo a defining modulus m, with denominator m^dim(V). It equals the product of normalized prime-power densities only when the conditions are imposed independently at those primes; coupled CRT conditions use nu(S).

proofSteps: Average the finite-cover fundamental domain with its stabilizer multiplicities. Use GN.4 on each congruence translate in the main body.
Use the source cusp/reducibility estimate, including Lemma 12; integrate the explicitly normalized discriminant volume. Finite congruence conditions do not change the discarded error.
acceptance: Check the stated exponent and constant dependence; establish finiteness before using a natural cardinal.
Do not replace a uniform estimate by separate fixed-prime asymptotics.

Test coupled CRT conditions: the two residues (0 mod 3,0 mod 5) and (1 mod 3,1 mod 5) have density 2/15, whereas the product of their marginal densities is 4/15. Finite disjoint residue sums must retain this coupling.

nodes.title: Global-field finite-condition orbit count
nodes.statement: Fix a global field F, a nonempty finite S containing the archimedean places, and n in {2,3,4,5}. For n=3,4,5 use the representation G_n,V_n in Global Fields I Table 1. For n=2 use §9's affine representation V={x^2+a xy+b y^2}, with G={[[1,t],[0,lambda]]:lambda invertible} acting by change of variables; this model works also in characteristic two and at places above 2. Fix an S-local type sigma. Let Gamma be commensurable with G(O_S), let L be commensurable with V(O_S), and require Gamma to preserve L. Let F_G be a fundamental domain for Gamma in G(F_S). The generic Gamma-orbit count, weighted by 1/|Stab_Gamma(v)|, is vol_L(F_G(X)v_sigma)/|Aut(sigma)|+o(X). Number-field height regions have 0<|Delta|_S<X; function-field regions have |Delta|_S=X, with X tending to infinity through admissible norm values. Additive volume is normalized by the coefficient lattice. An invariant finite congruence subset of L multiplies this main term by its actual finite residue density; independently imposed prime-power conditions factor that density. Generic means the S_n-field condition, not just nonzero Delta.
hypotheses: Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.
proofSteps: Choose the S-arithmetic Siegel set and invariant bounded-height slice. Generic means the field/Galois-group condition in this representation, not merely nonzero discriminant.

Use the lattice estimate on a compact truncation, the coordinate cusp estimate and finite splitting-type sieve to discard nongeneric points. S-adic measure and reduction-theory interfaces are gap G-global.

Keep weighted counts and the source function-field norm shells. For n=2 the bounded fundamental region and nonreductive Haar/Jacobian computation are §9.2 and §9.4 inputs; Table 1's G_m model cannot parametrize characteristic-two quadratic extensions.
acceptance: Check the stated exponent and constant dependence; establish finiteness before using a natural cardinal.
Do not replace a uniform estimate by separate fixed-prime asymptotics.

nodes.title: Global-field uniform tail estimate
nodes.statement: For the fixed global field, S and native representation of the preceding count, first take the standard arithmetic lattice V(O_S) and group G(O_S). At each prime p outside S let W_p be the union of rings nonmaximal at p and rings with extra ramification there, in the intrinsic ring-theoretic sense of Global Fields I §5. Then sum_{N(p)>M} N(W_p;X)=O(X/(M log M))+o(X), for M>=2, using stabilizer-weighted generic orbit counts and the same number-field regions or function-field norm shells. The O constant is independent of M and the negligible term is uniform for the sieve limit. Extension to a fixed Gamma-stable commensurable lattice requires a finite-index/denominator comparison; it is recorded in G-global. For quadratic rings use the §9 model; there is no extra-ramification locus in that case. In characteristic two this is a maximality sieve, not an ordinary-discriminant squarefree sieve.
hypotheses: Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.
proofSteps: The extra-ramification locus W_p^(2) reduces into a fixed codimension-two scheme; apply the S-arithmetic geometric sieve outside finitely many exceptional primes.

The nonmaximal but not extra-ramified locus W_p^(1) admits local maximalization, a discriminant decrease by N(p)^2, and at most 10 orbit preimages. Use the finite ideal-class lattices and sum prime-ideal reciprocal squares. These intrinsic loci are not the polynomial strong/weak partition in characteristic two.
For n=2 use the change-of-generator argument of §9.3: nonmaximality yields a in p and b in p^2 after a local group move. Record the separate group and fixed-lattice comparison adapters in G-global.
acceptance: Check the stated exponent and constant dependence; establish finiteness before using a natural cardinal.
Do not replace a uniform estimate by separate fixed-prime asymptotics.

With stabilizer-weighted generic orbits and the same function-field norm-shell convention, N(Z;X)=vol_L(F_G(X)v_sigma)/|Aut(sigma)| times product_{p outside S} vol(Z_p)+o(X). nodes.statement: Let G act integrally on V of positive rank r and let f be a primitive geometrically squarefree relative invariant of positive degree d.
